newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Monday on speculative buying, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,415 yuan ($412) per tonne, rising 35 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 3,450 and hit a low of 3,385.
May rose 25 yuan to 3,414, July 25 to 3,390, November 14 to 3,410, the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,405 and March put on 15 to 3,395.
Combined volume fell slightly to 16,100 tonnes from 16,300.
"Speculative buying dominated today's trading but its upward potential is limited due to a lack of fresh capital," one trader said.
"There was no market-moving news to support today's rises, which resulted in little follow-up buying," another trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around the 3,400-yuan level in the short term with most investors being more interested in the more active stock market.
